visual.general_description: Seven-panel composite figure labeled a to g: pelvic CT, ultrasound, two fluoroscopic images, an endoscopic view, a follow-up CT and an operative photograph.
visual.detailed_description: Panels a and b form the top row (CT and ultrasound), c, d and e the middle row (two fluoroscopic images and an endoscopic color view), and f and g the bottom row (CT and an operative photograph with a yellow circle). Each panel carries a bold white-on-black letter. The only other printed text is small device text at the top right of the ultrasound panel.

panels.general_description: Grayscale axial CT image through the pelvis with a large low-attenuation region anterior and a rounded low-attenuation collection posterior to it.
panels.detailed_description: Axial grayscale CT slice at the level of the iliac bones, which appear as bright bone on both sides, with the sacrum and coccyx at the bottom. A large low-attenuation rounded structure lies anteriorly in the midline. Behind it, a smaller rounded low-attenuation collection with a slightly irregular wall sits in front of the rectum, and a small black gas focus is visible near the posterior midline. The soft tissue around these structures appears hazy. The bold letter a is printed at the bottom left. No measurement markers or other printed text are visible.

panels.general_description: Grayscale B-mode ultrasound image with a dark anechoic region at the top and a rounded speckled hypoechoic region below.
panels.detailed_description: Fan-shaped grayscale ultrasound image. A large dark triangular region lies in the upper part beneath curved layered tissue. Below it is a rounded, well-circumscribed region with fine speckled mixed echotexture and a thin darker rim, surrounded by brighter echogenic tissue. A bright echogenic area extends beneath it. Small device text beginning LOGIQ with a short code beneath is printed at the top right, and the bold letter b is at the bottom left. No patient name or date is visible.

panels.detailed_description: Hazy grayscale fluoroscopic view. The banded radiodense endoscope shaft runs up the left edge to a rounded metallic tip. From the tip region a thin radiolucent tube with small bright loop-like ends extends to the right and slightly upward, and two short tubular segments with small rings lie just above the tip. Faint contrast opacification is visible in the upper part and faint pelvic bone outlines below. The bold letter d is at the bottom left. The exact number of catheters cannot be distinguished with confidence.
